column3: ms   (English and Malay for the sample string tables; salam_neighbours is left untranslated on purpose)

column2: Find 3 ripe mangoes for Auntie Daeng at the market
column3: Cari 3 biji mangga masak untuk Mak Cik Daeng di pasar

column2: Tip: the night market opens after sunset
column3: Petua: pasar malam dibuka selepas matahari terbenam

column2: Sweet, fragrant ripe mango. Restores 20 HP. Used for mango sticky rice.
column3: Mangga masak yang manis dan wangi. Memulihkan 20 HP. Boleh dibuat pulut mangga.
Gerai Mak Cik Daeng · Pasar malam

column2: A woven coconut-leaf case: fill with rice and boil. Eaten with curry on Raya and shared with neighbours of every faith.
column3: Sarung daun kelapa yang dianyam: isi dengan beras dan rebus. Dimakan dengan kari pada hari Raya dan dikongsi dengan jiran semua agama.

column2: Saturday morning: the village market is busier than ever.
column3: Pagi Sabtu, pasar kampung lebih sibuk daripada biasa.

column2: Ton, dear, perfect timing! Can you help me deliver to three customers?
column3: Ton, kebetulan sungguh! Boleh tolong Mak Cik hantar barang kepada tiga pelanggan?
Tiga orang pelanggan, Mak Cik Daeng?

column2: Mango sticky rice for the monk, morning glory for Uncle Mee, and the balm the headman is sending to Grandpa Phoem.
column3: Pulut mangga untuk sami, kangkung untuk Pak Cik Mee, dan balsem kiriman ketua kampung untuk Tok Phoem.

column2: Sure! I'll take care of it.
Thank you, dear. Here's ten baht of snack money.
column3: Terima kasih, nak. Ini sepuluh baht duit belanja.

column2: Can I grab a smoothie first?
Be quick, the sticky rice will go cold.
That's all right, dear. Come help me another day.
column3: Tak apa, nak. Lain kali datang tolong Mak Cik, ya.

column2: Ton runs past the noodle shop all the way to the temple.
column3: Ton berlari melepasi kedai mi sampai ke hadapan wat.

column2: Blessings, Ton. You're here early today.
column3: Selamat pagi, Ton. Awal kamu datang hari ini.

column2: Auntie Daeng sent this mango sticky rice as an offering.
column3: Mak Cik Daeng kirim pulut mangga ini sebagai persembahan.

column2: Thank you. Please pass my thanks to Auntie Daeng.
column3: Terima kasih. Sampaikan terima kasih saya kepada Mak Cik Daeng.

column2: My morning glory is here? I thought she'd forgotten.
column3: Kangkung Pak Cik dah sampai? Ingatkan dia terlupa.

column2: Give the morning glory to Uncle Mee
column3: Beri kangkung kepada Pak Cik Mee

column2: Thanks, kiddo. Take a mango to Grandpa Phoem for me.
column3: Terima kasih, cu. Bawakan sebiji mangga untuk Tok Phoem.

column2: Sneak a taste of the morning glory
Sorry, Uncle... I was just a little hungry.
column3: Maaf, Pak Cik... saya lapar sikit.

column2: Ton! You're running so fast. Where are you off to?
column3: Ton! Lajunya berlari. Nak ke mana?

column2: To Grandpa Phoem's, Fon. {delivered} done, one more to go.
column3: Ke rumah Tok Phoem, Kak Fon. Dah hantar {delivered}, tinggal satu lagi.

column2: Uncle Mee sent you a mango, Grandpa.
column3: Pak Cik Mee kirim mangga, Tok.

column2: What a kind boy. Here's five more baht for snacks.
column3: Baiknya budak ini. Tok beri lima baht lagi untuk belanja.

column2: Thank you, dear. Go home safely and watch out for cars.
column3: Terima kasih, cu. Balik elok-elok, hati-hati dengan kereta.

column2: All {delivered} delivered. Well done, Ton! You earned {coins} baht today.
column3: Semua {delivered} sudah dihantar. Syabas, Ton! Hari ini kamu dapat {coins} baht.

column2: Yay! I'll come help again tomorrow!
column3: Yay! Esok saya datang tolong lagi!

column2: You haven't finished the deliveries yet, Ton.
From the headman for Grandpa Phoem
column3: Kiriman ketua kampung untuk Tok Phoem

column2: Uncle Mee's gift for Grandpa Phoem
column3: Kiriman Pak Cik Mee untuk Tok Phoem

column2: Auntie Daeng has orders for three customers. Delivered {delivered}/3.
column3: Mak Cik Daeng ada pesanan untuk tiga pelanggan. Sudah dihantar {delivered}/3.

column2: Take the job from Auntie Daeng
column3: Terima tugas daripada Mak Cik Daeng

column2: Talk to Auntie Daeng at the market
column3: Bercakap dengan Mak Cik Daeng di pasar

column2: Offer the mango sticky rice to the monk
The temple is to the north-west
column3: Wat terletak di arah barat laut

column2: Bring the morning glory to Uncle Mee's field
column3: Hantar kangkung ke sawah Pak Cik Mee

column2: Take Uncle Mee's mango to Grandpa Phoem
column3: Bawa mangga Pak Cik Mee kepada Tok Phoem

column2: Bring the balm to Grandpa Phoem
Saving up for a smoothie. {coins} baht so far.
column3: Mengumpul duit untuk beli jus. Setakat ini {coins} baht.

column2: Ton promised to help Auntie Daeng at the market again tomorrow.
column3: Ton berjanji akan menolong Mak Cik Daeng di pasar lagi esok.

column2: Help Auntie Daeng set up her stall
column3: Tolong Mak Cik Daeng menyusun gerai

column2: Rice porridge for breaking the fast, made by Kak Na
column3: Bubur untuk berbuka puasa, air tangan Kak Na

column2: Break the fast with dates and water
Auntie Daeng's gift to share at the mosque
column3: Kiriman Mak Cik Daeng untuk dikongsi di masjid

column2: A woven coconut-leaf case for cooking rice on Raya
column3: Sarung daun kelapa yang dianyam untuk menanak nasi pada hari Raya

column2: A bamboo oil lamp lit outside the house the night before Raya
column3: Pelita buluh yang dinyalakan di depan rumah pada malam Raya

column2: Help Kak Na and Auntie Daeng bring iftar food to the mosque.
column3: Tolong Kak Na dan Mak Cik Daeng menghantar juadah berbuka ke masjid.

column2: Bring the bubur and pomelo to the mosque yard
column3: Bawa bubur dan limau bali ke halaman masjid

column2: The wooden mosque is north-east, past the market
column3: Masjid kayu di arah timur laut, selepas pasar

column2: Hand the dates to Pak Ismail
Stay until it is time to break the fast
After sunset you will hear the azan from the mosque
column3: Selepas matahari terbenam azan akan berkumandang dari masjid

column2: {ketupat}/3 ketupat woven. Light the pelita tonight.
column3: Sudah anyam {ketupat}/3 ketupat. Nyalakan pelita malam ini.

column2: In the yard in front of the tadika
Help Kak Fatimah light the pelita
Give Raya greetings, ask forgiveness, then share ketupat with the neighbours.
column3: Ucap selamat Hari Raya, bermaaf-maafan, kemudian kongsi ketupat dengan jiran.
Ucap selamat Hari Raya kepada Adam

column2: Bring ketupat to Grandpa Phoem and Auntie Daeng
column3: Bawa ketupat kepada Tok Phoem dan Mak Cik Daeng
